key_insight: Symmetry-preserving quantum circuits can retain hidden invariant blocks that limit target-state fidelity, but algebra-guided generator additions can remove these accessibility barriers.
engineering_relevance: Screening candidate gates before variational optimization can guide symmetry-preserving circuit extensions toward better state accessibility.
method: Compute the residual dynamical Lie algebra and its commutant to identify invariant blocks and fidelity bounds.
Screen added generators by the blocks they couple and the adjoint modules they generate.
Use real-rotation and complex-escape criteria to expand controllability; guide multi-block design with a connected coupling graph.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports algebraic proofs and demonstrations in XXZ and Hubbard models, but provides no numerical performance metrics.
watch_item: Removing algebraic accessibility barriers does not by itself guarantee shallow circuits, noise robustness, or successful variational optimization.
paper_title: Residual-Algebraic Design of Symmetry-Preserving Variational Quantum Circuits
